subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should OpenClaw add default bounded Docker sandbox control-plane waits and fail-soft sandbox unavailability behavior for wedged Docker/OrbStack cold starts, and if so what config/default boundary should ship?
rationale: The source-level hang is real, but the final timeout value, whether it is configurable, and how fail-soft behavior should affect slow Docker setups are compatibility-sensitive choices that automation should not settle.

options.title: Refresh or replace timeout/fail-soft fix
options.body: Bound the full sandbox Docker prep path, preserve current workspace mount behavior, document any config/default, and require real wedged-Docker or OrbStack proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Accept a narrower Docker exec mitigation
options.body: Land a smaller deadline around selected Docker init calls while explicitly accepting remaining prune/hash/live-proof gaps as follow-up work.

options.title: Decline core behavior change
options.body: Treat this as an external Docker/OrbStack operator condition and document mitigation instead of changing sandbox runtime defaults.

recommendation.title: Refresh or replace timeout/fail-soft fix
recommendation.body: Bound the full sandbox Docker prep path, preserve current workspace mount behavior, document any config/default, and require real wedged-Docker or OrbStack proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans sandbox runtime architecture, operator defaults, and fail-soft product behavior rather than only the Docker helper implementation.
